stage1.impression: A shallow-focus tabletop detail at the bar: a coupe, a dark mixing glass, a bottle, a turntable under a smoked lid, and a clear tube of stacked coloured coins on a black base. Behind them a soft grey speaker sits in a fir shelving wall. The warm grade and the depth of field are convincing at a glance. At 1:1 it gives itself away as CG: the counter is a large blotchy stain map that reads as printed marble rather than concrete, the turntable's slabs are flat grey bands with razor edges, the empty top of the tube reads as an opaque white cylinder, and there is speckle noise in the darks. The column and the coins make it read as a specific place, but the room behind could be any bar's shelving, and the speaker beyond is a dull grey blur, not a hero. A magazine would not run it as is; it reads as a nice render of a bar detail.

blocking_9: Counter top reads as real board-formed or cast concrete at 1:1 (fine aggregate, low-contrast staining at real scale, soft sheen), not a large-scale blotch map
The empty upper part of the request column reads as clear thick acrylic with polished glowing edges and clean reflections, not an opaque white cylinder (median now 173)
The EARF speaker beyond is legible and tinted, with light reading through its acrylic (region median >= 60, not grey)
No visible speckle or grain in the darks (bottle, mixing glass, back wall)
Lower-left turntable slab not crushed (crush_pct < 3) and its edges show a real material (a polished acrylic edge glow or a steel sheen), not flat grey bands
Foreground counter falls off darker toward the camera instead of brightening, so the eye lands on the drink and the column
Clean framing: the votive, napkin and sleeve not cut by the frame edges, and the coupe stem not cutting the bottom edge on a white napkin corner

Answer to 'specific or generic': a magazine would read it as specific only through the column and the coins. The background needs one recognisable element of this room (record wall spots, a niche glow, fir beam detail) in focus range to stop the back reading as generic shelving

defects.what: The concrete counter is a stretched, high-contrast blotch texture that reads as printed stone or marble. No aggregate, no pour lines, and the scale is wrong. Median 86, and it gets brighter toward the camera
The empty upper part of the request column reads as a solid milky white cylinder (lum_median 173), not clear acrylic
The background speaker is grey and colourless (r/g/b medians 59/48/36), with no tint and no light through its acrylic. Median 49, just at the floor for the hero
The turntable's lower slab and base are crushed (crush_pct 10.5) and the upper bands are flat grey with CG-sharp edges. The smoked lid reads thin
The mixing glass is nearly black (median 24) and reads as empty dark glass with speckle noise inside
Speckle noise and grain on the bottle and the wall around it
The votive and its coaster are cut by the right edge of the frame
The record sleeve corner is cut by the right edge of the frame
The coupe's stem runs off the bottom edge onto a cut-off white napkin corner, and the stem bottom goes black
The column's base glow is a hard flat white band with no falloff onto the counter
The right half of the back wall is generic fir cubbies with nothing specific to this room

changes.problem: The counter reads as a printed blotch texture rather than concrete, and it is the largest surface in the frame.

evidence.measured: lum_median 85.6, p5 53 to p95 150 (range 97). Large dark/light stain patches 100 to 200 px across with no fine aggregate

change.setting: the concrete's tone and sheen (counter top)
change.from: high-contrast large stain map, light grey, matte-ish
change.to: stain contrast reduced by about 60%, stain map scaled down about 3x so it reads as fine aggregate and faint water marks, tone darkened one stop to a warm mid-grey, roughness about 0.45 with a soft sheen

changes.expected: The counter reads as honed cast concrete. Its range drops below 70 and its median to about 55 to 65, so the props stand out against it.

changes.problem: The counter gets brighter toward the camera, so the eye goes to the empty foreground instead of the drink and the column.

evidence.measured: y profile rises from 68.5 to 92.0 toward the bottom edge

change.setting: the Domes' downlights (the one over the decks)
change.to: 60 W, cone 22 deg, re-aimed about 0.3 m away from the camera onto the column and coupe

changes.expected: A pool of light on the column and drink that falls off toward the lens. The bottom band is darker than the band through the props.

changes.problem: The empty top of the request column reads as an opaque white cylinder rather than thick clear acrylic.

evidence.measured: lum_median 173, p5 120: uniform milky white with no see-through to the background

change.setting: how rough the frosted acrylic is (the request column's tube)
change.to: roughness 0.02 clear, so only the polished edges carry the base light up as two thin glowing lines

changes.expected: The upper tube shows the dark background through it, with two bright edge lines. Its region median drops below 110 and the range widens.

changes.problem: The EARF speaker beyond is a grey colourless blur rather than a tinted acrylic hero.

evidence.measured: lum_median 49.4; r/g/b medians 59/48/36, close to the neutral wall

change.setting: the lamps on the speakers (on each speaker, 4 x area)
change.to: 2.5 W/m2 at the target, 2900 K, with one of the four placed behind the cabinet so light passes through the smoked acrylic

changes.expected: The speaker reads as glowing smoked acrylic with the batts visible, clearly brighter than the shelving around it.

changes.problem: The turntable's lower slab is crushed and its bands are flat, so the record player reads as a CG box.

change.setting: the candles (counter, 2 x point) plus grade
change.from: 3.0 W, 1900 K; look AgX - Medium High Contrast
change.to: move one candle votive to about 0.25 m in front of the record player's left corner at 4.0 W, 1900 K; look AgX - Base Contrast

changes.expected: A warm edge glow along the slab's polished acrylic edge and readable shadow detail in the base.

changes.problem: The mixing glass is a near-black void and does not read as a drink just made.

change.from: dark, empty-looking glass with a spoon
change.to: a clear mixing glass with large clear ice, a little amber liquid left, and the right-hand votive set just behind it so the ice backlights

changes.expected: The ice and glass catch small warm highlights, and the glass reads as clear, not black.

changes.problem: The frame edges cut the votive, the sleeve and the napkin, and the coupe stem runs off the bottom.

evidence.measured: votive and coaster clipped at the right edge; sleeve corner clipped at [1030,480,1200,590]; napkin cut at the bottom [300,740,470,800]

change.to: position about 0.15 m further back along the view axis and 0.03 m higher, lens 40 mm, f/2.8 kept, still focused on the column [7.5, 4.01, 1.17]

changes.expected: The coupe stands whole on its napkin, and the votive and sleeve sit inside the frame or are deliberately left out.

changes.problem: Speckle noise in the darks reads as render noise rather than film grain.

evidence.measured: visible salt-and-pepper speckle on the bottle and the wall at 1:1 (and in the mixing glass)

change.to: samples 768, adaptive 0.01, no added grain (add a fine, low-amplitude grain only after denoising if needed)

changes.expected: Clean darks with only fine, uniform grain.

out_of_scope.request: Tint the EARFcoins in the Smoke configuration, or reduce their range of colours, so the only saturated colour in the frame comes from EARF's speaker
out_of_scope.why: The coins are an EARF product whose colours are fixed by the card. Right now their multicolour stack competes with the speaker as the frame's colour

out_of_scope.request: Give the R3 Float's slabs thicker, polished glowing edges
out_of_scope.why: The record player's shape and parts are fixed

out_of_scope.request: Replace the generic fir cubbies at the back right with something specific to the room
out_of_scope.why: The back bar and record wall are fixed room design. Only their light (the record wall's spots) can change
